4. Similarly in Civil Revision Case No. 1031 of 1987 (Dhaka) renumbered as Civil Revision No. 285 of 1988 (Rangpur), the opposite parties Nos. 1,15as plaintiffs filed O.C. Suit No. 181 of 1982 in the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge, Bogra on 2.7.82 against the present petitioner for a declaration that an ex parte decree passed on 4.1.80 in O.C. Suit No. 17 of 1979 is void, illegal and fraudulent and prayed for cancellation of the same. This suit was valued at Taka 12,600/- only when the pecuniary jurisdiction of the learned Munsifs now Assistant Judges was Taka 6,000/- and Taka 10,000/- only. But subsequently the same has been raised upto Taka 20,000/- and 50,000/- by virtue of the said Civil Court's (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983. In pursuance of the said amendment, the learned District Judge by his aforesaid order dated 19.5.87 under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure transferred the instant suit from the Court of the learned Subordinate Judge Bogra to the Court of the learned Assistant Judge, Kahaloo, within his district for trial and disposal. 

 (2) Notwithstanding any amendment made by this Ordinance in the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 (Act V of 1908), an appeal from an appellate decree or an application for re- vision under section 115 which was pending before the High Court Division immediately before such amendment takes effect shall be continued and disposed of in accordance with the provisions of that Code as was in force before such amendment, as if no such amendment had been made.
